en: The Sūtra of the Most Victorious and True Names and Meanings of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Imperial Edict by the Dharma Master of the Tripiṭaka, Śārapa, who held the rank of Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of Works.
Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Auspicious Vajradhara, you who can subdue those difficult to tame,
heroic one who surpasses the three realms, sovereign Lord of Secrets.
With eyes like blue lotus petals and a face as full as a lotus flower,
he wields the vajra; with his hand he hurls it again and again,
manifesting frowning expressions and other forms— boundless Vajradharas.
There is also the subduer of evil māras, Majestic and fierce, inspiring great awe;
He emits the blazing light of the great vajra, Hurling the vajra-pestle with great compassion and great wisdom,
Using skillful means to benefit all sentient beings.
Some leaped for joy, while others manifested wrathful forms;
all followed the teachings of the Buddhas and went in person to the place of the World-Honored One to prostrate before the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Joining my palms in reverence, I crouch before you and speak these words:
"O Lord of the Universe, may you look upon me with compassion;
for the sake of benefiting us, please employ the net of illusory manifestations so that I may realize awakening."
For those who lack wisdom and are deluded, drowning in the afflictions and hardships—
may he likewise bring such as these to the realization of the unsurpassed fruit,
the ultimate perfect enlightenment; may the World-Honored One, the Tamer and Teacher, [grant this].
Thoroughly realizing the samaya, the Bhagavān of the Wisdom Body who knows the faculties,
dispositions, and natures; born from the great wisdom of Mañjuśrī, the Lord of Speech, the Wisdom-Syllable (jñānakūṭa).
Proclaiming the most supreme name, the profound, vast,
and tranquil meaning of the Great Dharma which is peerless— excellent in the beginning, middle, and end,
as already taught by past Buddhas and to be taught by future Buddhas.
The Buddha of the present now speaks this great teaching, the net of illusory transformations, which is thus throughout the three times.
Vajrapāṇi, the holder of secrets, and the immeasurable assembly rejoice; we pray that you will proclaim these wondrous sounds.
The Buddha has spoken these secret words; we are able to receive and uphold them with a resolute and firm mind.
Until the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, we shall act to extinguish all afflictions and sever both ignorance and wisdom.
In accordance with the diverse capacities of beings, I pray that you will teach the most supreme Dharma.
Having addressed the World-Honored One in this way, Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
joined his palms in reverence and stood before him with devotion.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, the supreme among two-legged beings,
extended his broad and long tongue from within his face,
filling the entirety of the three realms and subduing the hosts of the four Māras.
To eliminate the evil destinies, he manifested a smile and further issued a beautiful Brahma-voice that resounded throughout the three realms,
praising the Lord of Secrets, the Greatly Powerful Vajrapāṇi.
Out of great compassion, you have earnestly exhorted [me] to speak for the vast benefit of all living beings;
this wisdom-meaning of Mañjuśrī is named "Purifying All Defilements of Sin," the supreme and ultimate benefit.
Praising him, he said: "O Vajrapāṇi, excellent, most excellent!
For you, O Lord of Secrets, I shall now speak well;
listen with a single mind and attend closely. "So be it, Blessed One," [he replied].
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha revealed the secret Dharma,
the lineage of the holders of secret vidyā-mantras, the lineage of the three families of contemplative observation,
and the great lineage that universally illumines the mundane and supramundane.
The Mahāmudrā, the Supreme Seed; the Uṣṇīṣa Seed—these and more constitute the introductory section, totaling twenty-four verses.
The Gāthā words and phrases are the masters, the six kinds of Secret Mantra Kings.
Arising through non-dual correspondence, he proclaims the dharma of non-arising.

Ā Ā (1) E Ī (2) U Ū (3) I Ī (4) O AU (5) AṂ AḤ (6). SIDDHĀNTA (1) JÑĀNAMŪRTI RĀŚIPUṆYADHĀTUN (2) MŪDHAJÑĀNA (3) TĀRGARATNAN (4). OṂ VAJRĀKṢAṆADURGAṬI KṢETRAJÑĀMŪRTIDHĀTIN (1) JÑĀNAGAYA (2) VAGIŚVARA (3) ARAPACANAYATE NAMO (4). This concludes the three verses of the *Māyājāla*.
Thus, O Bhagavān, the syllable *a* is born from the syllable *bodhi*;
the syllable *a* is supreme. It is the subtle syllable of great meaning, the great birth whose meaning is non-arising, and which is far removed from the characteristics of speech.
The cause of the excellence of sound, Which can manifest all verbal characteristics;
Great desire is a great offering, By which all sentient beings rejoice;
Great anger is a great offering, The great enemy of all afflictions.
Great Delusion is the Great Offering; The Mind of Delusion removes ignorance.
Great Wrath is the Great Offering; It removes great enmity and harm.
Great Desire is the Great Offering; It is able to eliminate all cravings and desires.
Great desire and great bliss, Great joy and great passion,
Great form and great body, Great marks and great child,
Great name and great vastness— The vast and extensive maṇḍala.
Wielding the great sword of wisdom, possessing the great hook that overcomes great afflictions;
bearing a great name and great renown, a great light and great radiance that illuminates;
holding great skillful intelligence and great illusion, manifesting the signs of the perfected meaning of great illusion.
The Great Illusion, the Most Sublime Joy; the Great Illusion who bestows illusory emanations, the Supreme Honored One of Great Generosity;
whose ethical discipline is the greatest, and whose patience is firm; possessing great vigor and heroic valor.
Abiding in great dhyāna and meditative absorption, possessing a body sustained by great prajñā and great power,
and endowed with great skillful means; an ocean of great vows and great wisdom,
whose nature is immeasurable great loving-kindness, and whose body of great compassion is most sublime.
Prajñā possesses great wisdom, Great skillful means, great supernormal powers, and great strength;
It is courageous, swift, and renowned for its great supernormal transformations;
It is of great power, the great adversary, and the great enemy.
Destroyer of the mountain of the three realms of existence, Wielding the vajra,
fierce, great, and heroic; Causing great terror and fear,
O Venerable One of the most excellent lineage, Guru, Honored One of Secret Mantra.
Abiding in the principle of the Mahāyāna—the most supreme principle of the Mahāyāna.
The above is the "Praise of the Thirty-seven Bodhi-maṇḍalas," consisting of eighty-six names for the Vajra-bodhicitta, totaling twenty-four verses.
Mahāvairocana, the Great Tranquil One, the Great Muni,
born from the great secret mantra; having attained the ten pāramitās through the nature of the great secret, he abides in the ten pāramitās.
The ten pāramitās are purified; the Lord who is sovereign over the ten stages through the principle of the ten pāramitās— may I abide securely in the ten stages,
with my ten knowledges purified and my ten knowledges firmly established in purity.
The Meaning of the Ten Aspects and Ten Benefits: The Honored One of the Ten Powers, the Muni, brings benefit everywhere;
Possessing the ten great masteries, beginningless and free from conceptual proliferation, I and suchness are pure.
Speaking truth and speaking reality, speaking as it is and without deviation;
not teaching dualism, but non-duality; abiding in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), he lets out the lion’s roar of selflessness, shaking the wild beasts of the non-Buddhists.
Wandering through that which is meaningful, the Tathāgata of swift mind, supreme power, and conqueror of enemies;
the Great Powerful Wheel-Turning King, supreme among the hosts of teachers; the Honored One, the Great Sovereign.
The great multitude all revere and honor him; his Great Teaching is unsurpassed.
The Master of Speech is skillful in expression; as the Sovereign, he utters boundless words.
Speaking truthfully, he expounds the true meaning and proclaims the Four Noble Truths.
The non-retrogressive Anāgāmin, though the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas arise in various ways, share the same single true nature;
the Arhat, with outflows exhausted, is free from desire regarding the supreme faculties and objects.
Fearless, having attained peace and bliss, cool and free from afflictions,
perfect in knowledge and conduct; the Well-Gone One, knower of the world,
who is without self and does not grasp at a self, abiding in the principle of the two truths.
Having transcended the limits of saṃsāra, with all that was to be done already accomplished,
born of pure and singular wisdom, he destroys [delusion] with the sword of insight.
The light of the Dharma King of the True Dharma shines universally throughout the world.
The Dharma King, sovereign over the Dharma, proclaims the most excellent path that accomplishes all meaningful aims; free from all conceptual signs,
he reveals the inexhaustible realm of phenomena and the subtle, wondrous *dharmadhātu*.

Possessing merit, he cultivates the accumulation of merit; through wisdom, he gives rise to great knowledge and right cognition that realizes non-existence. He constantly and universally accords with the cultivation and gathering of the two provisions;
his meditative concentration and mind are subtle and wondrous.
Manifesting the physical form while remaining unmoving,
the supreme root of the three bodies and the nature of the five bodies of perfect enlightenment; pervading the nature of the five wisdoms,
adorned with the wondrous jewel crown of the five Buddhas, and possessing the five eyes, pure and unattached.
Increasing all perfect awakenings, O most excellent Son of the Buddhas, your wisdom does not arise within the three realms of existence. This Dharma can sever saṃsāra;
you are the one true nature of the vajra, born as the Lord of sentient beings.
Spontaneously arising from space, the great wisdom and great fire of intelligence shine forth with great light,
illuminating everywhere; the light of wisdom blazes intensely,
the world-lamp and great torch of intelligence, possessing great majesty and great radiance.
The Great Mantra of the Vidyārāja; the Great Meaning of the Secret Mantra, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Rare Uṣṇīṣa;
the manifestation of manifold forms within space, the selflessness of all Buddhas, endowed with the eye of worldly joy.
Increasing various forms, Making offerings and praises to the Great Sage,
Holding the secret mantras of the three families,
The Supreme Triple Gem speaks the supreme Three Vehicles— Amoghapāśa, the Victorious One.
Holding the vajra-noose and the great vajra-hook;
the above is the "One Hundred and Eight Names of the Vairocana Maṇḍala Praise for the Wisdom of the Pure Dharma-Dhātu," consisting of twenty-four verses, each with three lines.
The Terrifier of Vajra Terror, the wrathful king with six faces,
six eyes, and six arms of power; possessing the skeletal form,
bared fangs, a hundred faces, and a great laughing countenance— Yamāntaka, the King.
Vajrabhairava, Vajrasambhava, Vajraghoṣa, and Mahāmāyācitta;
Vajrodara, Vajreśvara, Vajragarbha, and Ākāśa; Acala and Ekajaṭī.
Clad in the hide of a great elephant, with a "ha ha" sound that is most fierce and a "hi hi" sound that is most terrifying; with a loud laugh and a roar, the sound of vajra-joyful laughter,
the Vajra Great Bodhisattva, the Vajra King, the Great Bliss.
Vajra-marked, great joy; holding the vajra-arrow with the vajra-mantra *hūṃ hūṃ*;
the sharp sword that severs afflictions;
vajra, vajra-marked; vajra that destroys the enemy armies.
Blazing vajra-eyes, with sharp and blazing hair raining down great vajras;
possessing a hundred vajra-eyes and a body covered in vajra-hair, with vajra-hair pervading his entire form.
Vajra-claws, sharp and keen; Vajra-treasury, firm skin;
Vajra-superior garland; Vajra-sublime adornment;
Hahaha, the great sound; the six-syllable Vajra-sound.
Mañjuśrī’s great voice pervades the three realms and extends even to the realm of empty space; his voice is most supreme.
[The above is the praise for the Maṇḍala of Akṣobhya Buddha, consisting of seventy-one names of the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom, totaling ten verses.]
The nature of suchness is selflessness; the limit of reality is beyond words.
You who speak of emptiness, Great Bull King, you blow the great conch of the profound and vast Dharma and strike the great drum of the Dharma.
Not abiding in nirvana, the drum of Dharma resounds throughout the ten directions;
formless yet manifesting wondrous signs, the mind-born displays various forms and auspicious rays of light, appearing as images without remainder.
Possessing supreme and great renown, the Great Sovereign of the three realms abides in the most excellent noble path; raising high the great Dharma banner,
he has the body of a youth of the three realms, yet bears the appearance of an aged World Lord.
Possessing the thirty-two marks, most sublime and majestic throughout the three realms, he is the Teacher who has thoroughly realized the world.
This Teacher of the world is fearless and acts as a refuge for the world; his protection is unsurpassed.
Enjoying the treasury of space, The ocean of all-knowledge wisdom,
He splits open the shell of ignorance, Tears asunder the net of birth and death,
Completely purifies all afflictions, And emerges across the ocean of saṃsāra.
Wearing the crown of wisdom-consecration, The Fully Enlightened One is adorned;
He has severed the three kinds of suffering, Attained the three kinds of liberation, And,
being far removed from all obscurations, Abides in a nature equal to space.
Transcending the defilements of affliction, all three times are likewise so;
The great dragons among sentient beings manifest atop the mountain of merit;
Liberated from all afflictions, they dwell victoriously in the path of space.
Holding the great wish-fulfilling jewel, the most supreme among all jewels;
a vast and great kalpa-tree that brings benefit to all sentient beings through the supreme vessel of the Great Sage,
providing benefit and happiness according to their needs.
Pure and penetrating, yet not limited to the pure; at the opportune moment, he masters the samādhis and thoroughly understands the faculties of sentient beings.
Skilled in the three doors of liberation, he possesses the penetration of merit and the penetration of Dharma—vast, great benefit, and auspiciousness.
Auspicious, most auspicious, renowned as auspicious, the cessation of fame, leaping with joy;
Great laughter and great bliss, served with reverence; Joyful praise, the Great Auspicious One.
The Great Giver, the Most Victorious Honored One, Subtle and Wondrous, worthy of refuge;
The Supreme Foe of great terror, Who eliminates all fears. Śikhin Śmaśānin, Jaṭī-muṇḍa-dhara.
Five-faced and five-crested, adorned with five topknots and flowers,
with a rounded crown and great diligence; upholding the supreme Brahma-conduct,
the exhaustion of suffering through great asceticism, the pure-dwelling Gautama.
Knowing the holy life, he practices the holy life;
having realized nirvāṇa, his body is liberated from bonds. Having attained the nature of liberation and tranquility, he realizes the extinction of nirvāṇa and swiftly attains wondrous parinirvāṇa.
Having decisively severed the extremes of suffering and pleasure, he has utterly abandoned all desires;
peerless and without equal, he is neither manifest nor attached, remaining unchanging and all-pervasive through his activity. He is the stainless, subtle seed.
Stainless and free from dust, pure; Free from loss, without fault or transgression, one awakens well to the Buddha-nature.
The omniscient one penetrates all, transcending the nature of consciousness; Non-dual wisdom is that which can be contemplated.
The perfected nature is non-conceptual; it is the practice of the perfectly awakened ones throughout the three times.
Perfect awakening has no beginning and no end; the primordial Buddha is without cause.
The single eye of wisdom is pure; this is the Tathāgata’s body of sublime gnosis.
The Great Speaker, the Sovereign Speaker, the Supreme Speaker, the King of Dharma—
unexcelled, incomparable, and peerless; with the unsurpassed lion’s roar,
he gazes upon all with universal joy, his garland of sublime majestic radiance.
With a sublime light and auspicious marks, his hand radiates pervasive brilliance;
he is a great and excellent physician, able to eliminate all suffering of disease.
He is also a wondrous medicinal tree that counteracts the enemies of all illnesses.
Majestic and sublime, transcending the three realms; The maṇḍala of the stars pervades the worlds of the ten directions.
Universally erecting the great Dharma-banner and spreading the great parasol, With compassion as the site of practice (bodhimaṇḍa).
Auspicious Lotus Dance, The Great Jewel Canopy that covers all,
The great majestic light of all Buddhas, Bearing the bodies of all the Perfectly Awakened Ones,
The great union of all Buddhas, The single teaching of all Buddhas.
Vajra-jewel initiation, sovereign lord of all jewels,
sovereign lord of the world; O Vajradharas,
the great mind of all Buddhas, you abide within the hearts of all Buddhas.
The great body of all Buddhas, Also the speech of all Buddhas,
the Vajra Sun Great Radiance, The pure light of the Vajra Moon,
free from desire yet possessing great desire, The blazing light of manifold colors.
The Perfectly Awakened One sits in the vajra posture, Holding the Buddha’s supreme ultimate Dharma;
The Perfectly Awakened Padmasambhava, Who upholds the treasury of omniscience,
And who holds all the kings of emanations— The Great Enlightened King of Vidyādharas.
The Greatly Beneficial Vajra Sword, the Pure and Supreme Syllable,
the Mahāyāna that Severs Afflictions; the Great Vessel of the Vajra Dharma,
the Profound Meaning of the Vajra, the Vajra Wisdom of the Definitive Meaning.
Perfected in the pāramitās, you adorn the stage of Buddhahood;
Pure in the dharma of selflessness, you are the moon of wisdom with supreme light and splendor.
Through the net of skillful emanations, you are the sovereign of all teachings.
The most supreme vajra-seat, the great Samantabhadra of wondrous wisdom who sustains all bodies of gnosis;
the Earth-Holding Lord of the World, the great Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas; he who manifests wheels and sustains all varieties.
The supreme nature of all natures, the sovereign holder of all natures,
the multitude of meanings of the unarisen dharma; the great wisdom that holds the self-nature of all dharmas,
awakening to all phenomena in a single instant.
Directly realizing all phenomena, the Muni abides in the true limit of reality and the nature of purity;
all Buddhas manifest before him as he attains perfectly complete enlightenment, a great wisdom-light of blazing radiance.
The above constitutes two hundred and seventy-five names of the Wondrous Contemplative Wisdom (*pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna*) from the *Amitāyus Buddha Maṇḍala Praise*, totaling forty-two verses.
Accompanying the body to accomplish wondrous meanings, Purifying all evil realms,
the Honored One who saves all sentient beings, Delivering and liberating all living creatures.
Alone he breaks the array of afflictions; He destroys delusion and pride, his wisdom supreme, upholding auspiciousness.
Firmly maintaining a formidable appearance, he moves with a hundred arms; His feet raised in a dancing posture.
The Auspicious One with a hundred arms dances throughout the entirety of space;
sometimes he rests upon it with a single foot as far as the limits of the golden wheel,
or extends a single toe to completely cover the realm of Brahmā.
In the single meaning there is no duality of phenomena; in the ultimate truth, phenomena are indestructible.

Various forms such as color and so forth, along with the mental consciousness, continue in succession within the emptiness that possesses signs; these are the two kinds of defiled attachment of the mind.
Having abandoned the defilements of the three realms of existence, you have attained the great bliss of the three realms;
like a pure cloud, like the bright moon of autumn,
and as wondrous as the orb of the rising sun, your fingernails possess the luster of red copper.
His jeweled crown is imperial blue; his jewel-tufted hair is a deep, great azure.
He possesses the auspicious light of maṇi-jewels, adorning the nirmāṇakāya Buddha who causes a hundred worlds to tremble, endowed with supernormal powers and great strength.
Maintaining one's own nature through right mindfulness, with the flowers and fragrance of the seven factors of enlightenment— the king of right concentration and the foundations of mindfulness—
one thoroughly understands the ocean of the Tathāgata’s virtues and the eightfold noble path, thereby accomplishing the way of perfect awakening.
Among all classes of sentient beings, you are unattached like space;

Within the minds of sentient beings, you give rise to [compassion]; You swiftly respond to the intentions of sentient beings, Thoroughly knowing their faculties and objects, And surpassing the minds of all sentient beings.
Having realized the true meaning of the five aggregates,
they see the five aggregates as pure and abide in the limit of arising;
skillfully giving rise to and dwelling upon the path toward arising, they universally demonstrate the dharma of arising.
Uprooting the twelve branches, the characteristics of the Four Noble Truths are purified in twelve ways;
from awakening arise the eight knowledges and the twelve true meanings,
which are the sixteen aspects of ultimate reality.
The twenty marks of perfect enlightenment— All Buddhas fully comprehend them;
The emanation bodies of all Buddhas, Appearing in infinite numbers,
Are realized and witnessed in a single thought-moment, Understanding all meanings in an instant.
Through various skillful means and vehicles, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings,
although the teachings of the three vehicles are proclaimed, the fruition abides in the single vehicle;
the realm of afflictions is purified, and all realms of karma are utterly eliminated.
Having already crossed the ocean of all sufferings— the afflictions and secondary afflictions born of associated activities—
and having completely eradicated habitual tendencies through great compassion,
wisdom, and skillful means, [he acts] for the benefit of sentient beings.
The meaning of severing all perceptions; the total cessation of the phenomena of consciousness;
contemplating the mentalities of all sentient beings; thoroughly understanding the minds of sentient beings and abiding in their mentalities;
entering in accordance with the inclinations of their minds.
Satisfying the intentions of sentient beings, causing them to rejoice,
and bringing them to fulfillment without ever becoming disordered; far removed from all erroneous understandings,
possessing the threefold meaning of non-doubting wisdom, and the nature of the three virtues of manifold benefit for beings.
The meaning of the five aggregates across three times— In a single thought-moment,
one can discern and realize awakening in an instant. Upholding the self-nature of all Buddhas,
the bodyless body, the wondrous body— One thoroughly understands the reality-limit of the body.
Manifesting all forms and images, the great jewel banner that fulfills wishes.
[The above is the praise of the maṇḍala of Ratnasaṃbhava Buddha. This section on the one hundred and four names of the Wisdom of Equality consists of twenty-four verses.]
All Buddhas have fully realized this supreme Great Bodhisattva mantra that is free from letters;
the meaning of the secret mantra born from the three natures of the great mantra, which is the Great Bindu free from letters.
The five-syllable gateway of Great Emptiness;
the bindu of emptiness, the hundred syllables, all marks being non-marks;
the sixteen half-and-half dots, beyond parts and transcending calculation; abiding above the four dhyānas.
Thoroughly penetrating the branches of meditative concentration, Fully understanding the fundamental cause of concentration,
The body of samādhi is most supreme, The enjoyment body is most excellent,
And the emanation body is likewise so; They maintain the nature of the Buddha’s transformations.
Pervading the realms of the ten directions, He transforms and delivers all sentient beings.
The God among Gods, neither god nor non-god,
The Teacher of the Eternal Lord of Heaven, The Great Sovereign who subdues Māra.
Having transcended the hardships of the three realms of existence, you alone are the Teacher of Gods and Humans,
whose fame pervades the ten directions. Acting as the great donor of the Dharma,
you wear the armor of steadfastness through the two dharmas of compassion and loving-kindness.
Wielding the sword and bow of wisdom, he destroys the army of the thieves of affliction and subdues the great evil Māras; having utterly eliminated the four obstacles of Māra,
he also brings low the hosts of demons— the Perfectly Awakened One who saves the world.
One should offer praise and prostrations; one should always draw near with reverence and serve him.
I bow my head to the Supreme Teacher, who in a single step transcends the three realms and universally subdues the entire expanse of space.
Pure and stainless with the three knowledges, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the six paths and six recollections,
Whose supernormal powers transcend the mundane and whose wisdom has reached the other shore, Realizing through wisdom the nature of suchness.
The perfection of one’s own and others’ awakening, a great *pudgala* beyond the reach of analogy,
the supreme Lord of Dharma whose wisdom is unknowable— He proclaims the meaning of the four seals.
Worthy of the veneration of gods and humans, Guiding through the pure and supreme meaning of the three vehicles, The Great Sage of the Three Realms,
endowed with all auspiciousness— Sublime Virtue, Supreme Auspiciousness!
The above constitutes the fifteenth verse, comprising ninety-five names of the *Amoghasiddhi-jñāna* (Wisdom of Accomplishing Activities) from the *Buddha-maṇḍala-stotra*.
I take refuge in the Great Victorious Bestower of Vajra; I take refuge in the principle of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*);
I take refuge in and prostrate to the one born of emptiness (*śūnyatā*); I take refuge in the unsurpassed Buddha-bodhi.
I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s beloved; I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s desire;
I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s joy; I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s great delight;
I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s right mindfulness; I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha’s joyful smile.
I take refuge and pay homage to the Buddha’s authentic speech; I take refuge and pay homage to the heart of all Buddhas;
I take refuge and pay homage to that which arises from the unborn; I take refuge and pay homage to the birth of all Buddhas;
I take refuge and pay homage to that which arises from space; I take refuge and pay homage to that which is born of wisdom.
I take refuge in the Supreme Māyājāla; I take refuge in the Great Play of all Buddhas;
I take refuge in all the Omniscient Ones; I take refuge and prostrate to the Body of Perfect Wisdom.

The above constitutes the concluding praise in one verse each for the Mirror-like Wisdom, the Wisdom of the Pure Dharma Realm, the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation, the Wisdom of Equality, and the Wisdom of Accomplishing Activities, respectively.
Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wields the vajra:
I shall now explain this pure, uncommon, and most excellent definition of the name of Mañjuśrījñāna, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
These are the bodies of true wisdom of all the World-Honored Ones, the Tathāgatas;
you should give rise to a mind of great, unsurpassed joy, purity, faith, and resolve.
All that pertains to the secrets of body, speech, and mind has not yet attained ultimate purity and perfection.
Furthermore, for those who have not yet understood the stages of the grounds,
the gates of the pāramitās, and the accumulations of merit and wisdom, he causes them to attain understanding;
and for those who have not yet attained realization, he causes them to attain realization.
It encompasses and sustains the entire Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas.
Therefore, I now analyze and explain it,
in order to bring about ultimate realization and understanding, and for the sake of its preservation.
Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
I shall embrace you within the fundamental nature through the natural dharmatā of all secret mantras.
The above constitutes twelve verses and lines concerning the merits of the first wheel.
O Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
you should now understand the most excellent meaning of the names.
This is the gateway of the three secrets of body, speech, and mind, purified by the knowledge of all-knowledge;
it is the true realization of the great samādhi of the perfect, complete enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
They skillfully enter the unsurpassed dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas;
these beings of supreme power subdue the forces of Māra and accomplish the meritorious qualities of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
It possesses the noble teachings of all dharmas, including omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*);
it accomplishes the pure and perfect accumulations of merit and wisdom of all Buddhas;
and it gives birth to the noble seeds of the three vehicles—great Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
It also causes human and celestial beings to dwell securely in the practices of the Mahāyāna bodhisattvas;
they enter the true, noble path and all attain liberation, never severing the lineage of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, it enables them to increase the assembly of noble bodhisattvas and to subdue those of external paths.
They destroy the four māras and gather in sentient beings;
they definitively bring them to maturity so that all may return to the Noble Path.
Abiding in samādhi, they practice the four brahma-vihāras.
While dwelling with the mind fixed on a single object in dhyāna,
one accomplishes the yogic actions of body, speech, and mind,
and is also able to eradicate both the root afflictions and the secondary afflictions.
One is then able to sever all fetters and bonds,
attain liberation from the aggregates, and pacify all distractions;
one produces the necessary requisites to universally relieve suffering and distress.
They close the gates to the evil realms and open the path to liberation;
they no longer enter the cycle of birth and death in saṃsāra,
but turn the great wheel of Dharma and establish the victory banner, flags, pennants, and parasols of the Tathāgata’s true teaching.
Abiding securely in the vast Dharma-teachings of the Tathāgata,
they swiftly accomplish all secret practice-gates of Bodhisattvas,
and further awaken to and diligently cultivate the samādhis of all Bodhisattvas.
In accord with the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Bodhisattva of Great Wisdom practices emptiness non-dually.
He is fully endowed with the treasury of all *pāramitās* and brings to perfection all the pure stages of Buddhahood.
The noble wisdom of the Four Noble Truths manifests before them;
they dwell with single-minded concentration in the four foundations of mindfulness,
until finally perfecting all the merits of the Buddhas.
The above constitutes the second wheel of merit, comprising fifty-two verses.
O Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
this most excellent meaning of the name is able to eliminate all evil, sinful, and defiled stains of the physical, verbal, and mental actions of all sentient beings.
One will also be able to distance oneself from all evil destinies and attain the severance of all karmic obstructions.
One shall never again be born in the eight states of no leisure; the eight fears shall be stilled, and all evil dreams and various ominous signs shall be dispelled.
It eliminates curses, spells, ghosts, demons, and obstacles;
it brings liberation from all maras, enemies, and fetters;
and it increases roots of goodness, merit, and benefits.
No longer will they give rise even momentarily to improper mental attention;
they will sever all forms of overweening pride, self-grasping, views, and the like,
and no sorrow, lamentation, suffering, or affliction shall arise.
It is also the heart-treasury of all Tathāgatas;
it brings about the thorough knowledge of the secret practices of Bodhisattvas as they truly are,
and the thorough knowledge of the seals, vidyās, and mantras that constitute the great secret modes of practice for Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
Having realized the meaning of the most supreme Dharma as it truly is,
one gives rise to great wisdom through right mindfulness and clear comprehension,
abiding in the practice of bliss with mastery over physical form and strength.
One shall obtain auspiciousness, security, purity, and the most excellent prosperity;
one shall attain great renown, and be extolled with beautiful verses and praises.
Furthermore, it can eliminate all diseases and great terrors.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to attain purity, they shall immediately attain purity; if they wish to achieve purification, they shall immediately achieve purification;
if they wish to attain abundance, they shall immediately attain abundance.
If one desires auspiciousness, one shall obtain auspiciousness.
If one desires a place of refuge, it shall become a place of refuge.
For those who have not yet attained the Way, it shall cause them to attain the stage of the Way.
He provides deliverance for those who have no deliverer;
he grants protection to those who have no protector;
and for those who seek a realm, he enables them to obtain a realm.
For those who wish to rely upon him, he serves as their reliance;
for those crossing the ocean of birth and death, he acts as their vessel;
and for those seeking to eliminate the suffering of illness, he is the Great King of Physicians.
Regarding the dharmas of adoption and rejection, he possesses the wisdom of discernment;
furthermore, through the illumination of his wisdom, he shatters the darkness of ignorance and false views.
This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrījñāna.
Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel fulfills all desires and benefits all beings,
so too does he truly comprehend the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Possessing the five eyes, he practices the giving of material wealth, the giving of fearlessness, and the giving of the Dharma, as well as the six perfections (ṣaṭpāramitā).
Having attained the four fearlessnesses and abiding in the ten stages,
they fully perfect the samādhi-gates of the great treasury of merit and wisdom, and realize the non-duality of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) as it truly is.
He understands the distinctions among the characteristics of form as they truly are;
he understands the purification of billions of various characteristics of form as they truly are,
because the intrinsic nature of the Tathāgata is entirely empty.
This most excellent name and meaning is the non-dual meaning of phenomena (*dharmārtha*).
If one upholds, reveals, and elucidates it,
one will be able to benefit all sentient beings.
He causes them to leave behind the dense forest of afflictions consisting of wrong views.
The above constitutes the fifty-two verses of the third wheel’s merits.
Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wields the vajra.

The Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrījñāna, is the supreme and most venerable embodiment of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas; his name and meaning are non-dual, like the great maṇi-jewel at the crown of a Buddha’s head.
If sons or daughters of good family desire to practice this,
they should rely upon this most excellent gateway of secret conduct and daily,
at the three periods of the day, recollect and contemplate the meaning of these verses.
With perfect and correct phrasing, one should receive, uphold, read, and recite [the teachings] without any confusion;
truly knowing the Dharma, one explains it for others.
Relying on each respective name, one should contemplate with utmost clarity the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Abiding in the practice of the Universal Gate, they receive it with single-minded faith and attain a mind of supreme resolve.
They thoroughly understand the most sublime ultimate meaning of all phenomena and realize unimpeded wisdom,
being fully able to comprehend the events of the three periods of time as well as that which has been from beginningless time.
Furthermore, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will appear before them,
giving birth to and revealing all dharma-gates.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas...
By means of body, speech, and mind, one is embraced within the reality of the fundamental nature;
one is blessed, benefited, and sustained by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas together.
They attain the fearless eloquence regarding all phenomena,
thoroughly penetrate all dharmas pertaining to śrāvakas, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas,
and are able to contemplate and realize the selfless nature of reality.
The Great Wrathful Kings who subdue all evils, such as Vajrapāṇi and others,
rescue the world and bring about great benefit,
manifesting various and infinite physical forms.
Possessing great radiance and endowed with all powers,
one is further able to accomplish all mantras and mudrās,
and directly realize the dharma of the samaya-maṇḍala.
All secret mantras and vidyā-mantras;
all the great Vidyārājas; all classes of evil māras; the Piṇāyakas; the evil māra-enemies; the Paṭṭadhāris; and the Mahā-Aparājitas.
They shall constantly provide protection throughout the day and night.

Furthermore, there are Brahmā, Śakra, Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, Kumāra, Maheśvara, Kārttikeya, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Yama-rāja, the water deities, the fire deities, Vaiśravaṇa, Hārītī, and even the deities who protect the worlds of the ten directions.

They shall constantly provide protection throughout the day and night—whether walking, standing, sitting, lying down, sleeping, or awake; whether dwelling in meditative concentration or having emerged from it—at all times they shall provide constant protection.

Whether dwelling alone in bustling marketplaces, or residing in royal cities, towns, villages, hamlets, alleys, empty houses, crossroads, gateways, mountain forests, rivers, or any other such place of habitation.
Whether in pure or impure places, or in states of heedlessness and the like,
they shall always be protected and constantly attain peace and security.
Furthermore, there are devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
And all the constellations, the assembly of Mātṛkās, the assembly of the Seven Mothers, the assembly of yakṣiṇīs, the assembly of piśāciṇīs,
and all the mātṛs of ghosts— such hosts together with their retinues.
One’s lifespan shall increase and one shall attain great auspiciousness.
The above constitutes nineteen verses regarding the merits of the fourth wheel.
Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wields the vajra.
If there should be one who, regarding this most excellent name and meaning— which is like a great maṇi-jewel from the Buddha’s uṣṇīṣa—
practices with diligence and without slackness three times each day,
single-mindedly upholding, transcribing, reciting, and reflecting upon it with right mindfulness;
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī is fully endowed with the physical marks and color of the wisdom-body.
By the power of this, one will before long swiftly behold the transformation bodies of bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, one shall behold all buddhas and bodhisattvas dwelling in the midst of space, manifesting immeasurable varieties of physical forms.
This great being shall never again fall into any of the evil destinies;
in the future, they shall not be born into a lowly lineage,
nor in a frontier region, nor with impaired faculties.
Furthermore, they will not be born into families of wrong views,
nor will they take birth in buddha-less lands;
being born in a land where a Buddha dwells, they will not abandon the True Dharma.
They shall never be born among the long-lived devas;
they shall not be born during kalpas of famine or warfare;
nor shall they be born in the evil world of the five turbidities.
In life after life, may they remain far removed from the perils of kings, thieves, and adversaries;
may they not be born into poverty or places of suffering and hardship;
and may they never hear words of contempt, slander, or abuse.
In birth after birth, may they be born into noble and virtuous families among those of high station;
may their physical form be perfect, upright, and complete,
such that there is none in the world who does not love and revere them.
In every place where they are born, all people rejoice to see them;
their speech is truthful and sincere, such that others trust and accept it;
they attain the knowledge of past lives and possess a great retinue.
Possessing great wealth that increases inexhaustibly,
they are fully endowed with the most supreme merits.
They are likewise fully endowed with the six pāramitās, as well as the intrinsic merits of the power of skillful means, vows, and wisdom.
He has fully perfected the four sublime abodes;
with right mindfulness and clear comprehension, he is fearless in all debates;
his speech is lucid and his eloquence is unimpeded.
Free from indolence, contented, and possessing few desires, they are further able to bring peace and comfort to all sentient beings.
They honor them with reverence no different from that shown to an ācārya or a teacher,
serving them in matters of craftsmanship, arts, supernatural powers, wisdom, and so forth.
Regarding the texts and doctrines of external treatises, both their words and their meanings,
he thoroughly mastered everything he had never heard before;
his conduct was pure, his life-span was long, and his observance of the precepts was complete.
Always delighting in leaving the household life, they attain full ordination for the sake of all-knowledge;
they never forget the great bodhicitta and no longer enter the realms of śrāvakas, arhats, or pratyekabuddhas.
The above constitutes fifty-two lines of verse regarding the merits of the fifth wheel.
O Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
because this most excellent name and meaning is endowed with immeasurable and boundless merit.
Furthermore, it can give rise to such an immeasurable and boundless accumulation of various merits.
O Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
if a son of good family truly upholds this most excellent "Meaning of the Names," [he shall attain these benefits].
It should be known that such a person will ultimately perfect the provisions of merit and wisdom,
swiftly fulfill all the qualities of a Buddha,
and before long realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Abiding in the world without entering parinirvāṇa,
for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
they raise the great banner of Dharma and beat the great drum of Dharma.
Acting as the Great Dharma King, he expounds the inexhaustible, unsurpassed, and wondrous Dharma.
He then spoke this mantra.
The above summarizes the merits of the five wheels.
At that time, Śrī-Vajrapāṇi, with joyful exultation, joined his palms and prostrated himself,
bowing his head in homage to the Bhagavān, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata,
the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Furthermore, O Venerable Lord of Secrets, the Great Vajrapāṇi, King of Wrath.
Together with the entire great assembly, they praised the Secret One, speaking these words:
"O World-Honored One, we are all filled with joy! Excellent, excellent!
You have skillfully expounded compassion, benefit, and [the welfare of] sentient beings, thereby accomplishing the fruit of Perfect Enlightenment."
The Buddha is the Great Teacher of the world, Guiding all to return to the path of liberation;
He proclaims the wondrous principles of the *Māyājāla*, All of which are pure and subtle paths.
These most supreme, vast, and profound meanings Universally bring benefit to the world.
"This is the holy realm of all Buddhas, proclaimed by all Tathāgatas.
(The above are the verses from the *Prasāraṇa* section.

On the ninth day of the twelfth month in the second year of Zhìdà, Lǐ Shēn Míngrén—abbot of Dàcíyīn Monastery in Guī'ān County, Húzhōu Prefecture—and Lǐ Zōngshè, who had been specially dispatched by the Imperial Prince’s decree via Hǎiyīn, an official of the Yánqìng Office, to the Jāngān Báiyún School to retrieve the scriptures, returned with the following: they were ordered to carefully carve woodblocks for printing these excellent manuscript copies of the *Sūtra of the Most Victorious True Names Spoken by the Buddha*, the *Buddha-spoken White Parasol Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, and the *Buddha-spoken Vajra of Destroying Appearances Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
I pay my respects to those who have entered the Great Canon for its circulation.

I humbly reflect that His Imperial Highness the Crown Prince, having planted roots of goodness in past lives, possesses a profound mastery of Buddhism; thus, in reverent compliance with his imperial decree, this work has been carved and printed for dissemination throughout the realm.
I reverently pray that the imperial domain may remain firm and secure, and that the Buddha-Dharma may spread and flourish, so that all who see or hear it may together attain the fruits of goodness.
Written on the [blank] day of the third month in the third year of Zhizhida, respectfully inscribed by Shen Mingren, Head of the Baiyun School.
